review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped Mathlib for other Fredholm definitions, for quasi-inverse notions and for topological-complement notions. Fredholm only appears in the sibling `Fredholm/Open.lean`, which imports this file, and in TODO or docstring mentions in `Banach.lean` and `ContinuousInverse.lean`. `IsFredholm` is the only Fredholm predicate in Mathlib, so it has no competitor. The file builds on existing Mathlib notions: `LinearMap.IsQuasiInverse`, `Submodule.IsTopCompl`, `ClosedComplemented`, `Submodule.CoFG`, `IsStrictMap`, `ContinuousLinearMap.IsInvertible`, `projectionOntoL` and `quotKerEquivRange`. `FredholmDecomposition` and `FredholmPackage` are bundled structures over `IsTopCompl` and finite dimensionality. They carry data that downstream code uses, such as `pkg.decDom.X₁` and `pkg.equiv` in `Open.lean`. Mathlib has no competing bundled version of them. The `IsFredholm` restate-lemmas (`isFredholm_subtypeL`, `isFredholm_projectionOntoL`, and so on) are named specialisations, not rival concepts. The Index section only restates `LinearMap.index_comp` for `IsFredholm`. I found no avoidable competing concept, so I abstain. The remaining uncertainty is limited to unrelated files I did not read in full.
